description:
Split out of fz-5xp.16 with authorization (user, 2026-09-07: 'we can skip them
for the moment'), so that ticket can close on what it set out to do.

fz has NO random number generator at all -- not a weak one, none. These three
Enum functions are the only callers the library has for one, which is why they
were grouped separately in fz-5xp.16's own breakdown from the start.

    random/1  shuffle/1  take_random/2

WHAT IT ACTUALLY NEEDS is a decision about the runtime, not library work:

  * where the seed lives. Erlang keeps per-process seed state in the process
    dictionary, so two processes that seed identically produce identical
    sequences and a process is reproducible on its own. fz has per-process
    heaps and no process dictionary.
  * which algorithm, and whether it is specified. Erlang's  names its
    algorithms (exsss, exro928ss) and documents that the default may change.
  * whether a fixture can pin anything. Every other fixture in this epic is
    oracle-checked against Elixir; a random one cannot be, so it has to pin
    DISTRIBUTION or REPRODUCIBILITY-from-a-seed instead, which is a different
    kind of test than the suite has today.

That last one is the reason this is not simply 'add a primitive'.
title: Enum: random/1, shuffle/1 and take_random/2 need an RNG fz does not have
